d4.name: cellAddr
d4.why: the cell being written, advanced by the routine itself with `addq.l #$1,d4` - so it is a running address and not a fixed one.

d2.name: cellValue
d2.why: masked to 0x3f before the owner bits are or-ed in, so only its low six bits - the kind - survive into the board.

d5.name: ownerBits
d5.why: or-ed into the top of the cell byte after the mask, which is the 0xc0 owner field the enclosure test, the flood fill and the piece walker all read.

d6.name: endMark
d6.why: the walk stops when the RAW cell byte at the address in d4 equals it (0x6576) - the whole byte, not the low six bits the dispatch at 0x635a masks off. Every entry of the family carries it.

d5.name: tileList
d5.why: a running pointer into a list of WORDS: `movea.l d5,a5` to read one and `addq.l #$2,d5` to step, so it walks two bytes at a time and each word is a tile handed to 0x11ef2.

d3.name: tableBase
d3.why: held in a data register and moved into a5 to be indexed by the owner times four, which is a table of longwords one per owner.

a5.name: ownerTable
a5.why: the table base moved into an address register to be indexed by the owner times four - a longword per owner, and the routine leaves at once when the owner is zero.

a2.name: coordRef
a2.why: dereferenced for a WORD which is pushed straight to the address computers 0x3cee and 0x3ba4 - so it points at a packed coordinate pair, not at a cell.

d4.name: at
d4.why: the screen address handed to the per-column decompressor at 0x11ef2, and replaced by nothing - the same argument goes to both calls.

a4.name: byteStream
a4.why: read with (a4) for a byte on the paths that need one, separate from the word list d5 walks.

d6.name: wantKind
d6.why: its low byte is compared at 0x3ad6 against the cell byte's low six bits - the kind - and the whole family branches away when they differ. Nothing else in the 346-byte extent touches it but the movem that restores it.
